the_day: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq in what outlets call the largest IPO on record, Google released Gemini 4 Neon and gave its Mac app computer use, Arizona and California took legal action over OpenAI's AI agents, new reports raised privacy questions about Meta's Muse, and xAI faced a new Grok image lawsuit.

items.headline: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq after the largest IPO on record
points: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq, which Forbes and Yahoo Finance put at 34% above the IPO price.
Reuters and The Guardian put the debut valuation near $2 trillion; Forbes said the gain narrowed to about 15% ahead of the close.
At the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei recommitted to pacing AI development, TechCrunch reports, and warned of 'very real risks' from AI.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, a lower-priced mid-tier model
points: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon; Notebookcheck says it replaces Argon for Google AI Pro subscribers.
TestingCatalog reports API pricing of $3 per million tokens; VentureBeat says Google claims Opus 5.5-level coding at 25% lower token prices.
SiliconANGLE reports Neon is three times faster than Gemini 4 Carbon and beats it on some metrics.
items.for_you: Google AI Pro subscribers now get Neon in place of Argon, and developers can use it in Google AI Studio.

items.headline: Reports say Muse mixed up conversations and read encrypted messages

Meta employees have raised privacy concerns about Muse internally, reports say; today's items include no response from Meta.
